title: fix-lsp configuration
description: Configuration for the fix-lsp server, sent under the `fix` section. Reusable by editor extensions (e.g. a VS Code `contributes.configuration`).

defaultVersion.description: FIX version used when a message has no (or an unknown) BeginString (tag 8).

name.description: Unique name within the applicable configuration chain; duplicate names are errors.

default.description: Make this definition the version default in this source's scope. FIX version comes only from XML.

dictionaries.description: External XML definitions require global allowDictionaryPath. Definitions accumulate under unique names; a stronger source may replace a version default under a distinct name.

messageSummary.description: Everything about the one-line message summary, including which LSP channels carry it.

channels.description: Document-overridable output channels, constrained by advertised client capabilities. Enabling both draws the summary twice.

rules.description: Built-in diagnostic rules. Unknown identifiers are non-fatal configuration errors and are ignored.

integrity.description: BodyLength and CheckSum, checked as one rule: they are recomputed from the same walk of the line and a repair fixes both, so two ids would be two ways to half-fix a message.

dictionaryVersion.description: Selected dictionary and resolved message version do not match; one finding per mismatching version in each diagnostic walk.

unknownMsgType.description: A MsgType(35) the line's dictionary does not list. Silent under a dictionary that lists no session message, whose table cannot be trusted to be complete. Only on a line whose dictionary was chosen, not fallen back to.

unknownTag.description: A tag the line's dictionary does not define, at every occurrence; says how standard FIX sees the tag as hover does. Only on a line whose dictionary was chosen, not fallen back to.

template.description: The message symbol's name. Same slots as messageSummary.template; fields, groups and instances are not templated.

url.description: Where a tag's reference page lives. `{tag}` is the tag number; `{version}` is the version as the default site spells it (`4.4`, `5.0`, `5.0.SP1`, `5.0.SP2`; FIXT.1.1 reads its `5.0.SP2` tables); `{fixVersion}` is the line's own version string (`FIX.5.0SP2`, `FIXT.1.1`). A template with `{version}` is linked only for a tag the bundled dictionary of that version defines; any other template links every tag, including a custom dictionary's own. A template that avoids `{version}` also works for versions the default site does not publish. Empty removes the link without disabling hover. Global-only; non-empty URLs must use http or https. Substituted values are percent-encoded.

overrides.description: Global-only source controls; a source cannot disable or enable itself.

rangeLines.description: Largest span of lines any ranged request will answer about: a code action, an inlay hint, an expanded selection, a coloured viewport. Each request decides for itself what happens past it.

semanticTokensFullLines.description: How many lines from the top a whole-document colouring answers about; past it the tail is uncoloured and one log line says so. 2000 is about 255000 tokens on a dense log, which is what a client can rebuild per response without a heap it cannot afford — the server itself colours the whole file in half a second.

documentSymbolItems.description: Largest number of symbols one outline may hold, the truncation marker included. A cap of zero cannot hold the marker it would need.

cachedLines.description: How many lines of one document may keep their analysis cached before the least recently read are dropped; never applied below rangeLines. About 440 bytes a line.

allowDictionaryPath.description: Global-only filesystem permission for every external dictionary. Project TOML and modelines cannot enable it.

format.description: How the label is written: literal text plus a nameless hole, {}. Each setting draws one thing, so the hole needs no name: for tagNames it is what the tag is called (its group path inside a group, unless groupPaths is off), for enumValues it is what the value means. An empty hole suppresses the whole label including its literals, which is why a tag the dictionary does not define is passed over; a format with no hole is therefore drawn on every field. Write a literal brace by doubling it; the hole may appear more than once and each repeats the same value. The label reaches the client verbatim, newlines included, and what it does with them is the client's.
